audit.summary: Archived assessment: Major. Equations (5.4), (5.14), and (5.15), on pp. 27 and 30, do not reproduce the mean-free control (3.9) on p. 18.; Lemma 4.2, p. 23, assumes \(g,h\in L^2((0,1);H^{m-1})\) but asserts convergence in \(H^m\), uniformly over bounded sets of those forces.; Theorem 5.1, pp. 27–28, asserts that one collection \((\zeta_l)_{l=1}^N\subset L^2(0,1)\) can be fixed so that \(w_\delta(\delta)\to w_1\) in \(H^k\) as \(\delta\to0\) for…
limitations: Counterevidence and alternatives: An implicit integral-chi=1 convention contradicts the actual partition identity.
Counterevidence and alternatives: The additional positive rescaling does not remove nonzero mean.

Counterevidence and alternatives: The argument grants time dependence of the y dot grad chi profile, so the demonstrated normalization error does not depend on resolving the separate profile representation issue.
Counterevidence and alternatives: This checks the printed construction for allowed controls; it does not prove nonexistence of some other successful control.
Counterevidence and alternatives: The return drift is retained exactly, not replaced by zero.
Counterevidence and alternatives: Nonlinear self-advection vanishes by the actual shear structure; it is not a linearization.
Counterevidence and alternatives: The constructed controls used later have more spatial regularity and might satisfy a suitably restricted scaling result.
Counterevidence and alternatives: Absolute continuity for a fixed h is distinct from uniformity over a bounded L2 family; source (5.10) is relevant to translated tails of one fixed h.
Counterevidence and alternatives: Direct smooth-data limit proof does not rely on the false general form of Lemma 4.2.
Counterevidence and alternatives: Controls depending on epsilon or delta avoid this fixed-control contradiction; those have different quantifiers.
Counterevidence and alternatives: The main theorem asks approximation at a prescribed tolerance, which this counterexample does not contradict.
Counterevidence and alternatives: The hypothesis is about chosen pointwise representatives, while the conclusion is L2; removable discontinuities cannot supply the required jumps.
Counterevidence and alternatives: The subsequent generating-drift theorem separately assumes observability, and valid observable families exist.
Limits: No historical-priority certification; findings do not refute the main approximate-controllability theorem.
Limits: The full generating-drift duality proof was read, not independently reconstructed in its entirety.
Limits: Only a bounded first-component period observation is retained as unresolved scope. No complete topological audit or additional graded defect.
The finding applies to the exact reviewed source version and inspected scope; uninspected publication versions are not adjudicated.
The report retains counterevidence and unresolved questions. Publication does not repeat scientific review.
Independent human scientific adjudication remains pending; author adoption has not been requested.

proposition.claim:
Recorded check: Equations (5.4), (5.14), and (5.15), on pp. 27 and 30, do not reproduce the mean-free control (3.9) on p. 18.

Normalized torus measure, nonnegative translated partition chi, K=36 covering squares with l=2pi/5, Fourier index set {(1,0),(0,1)}, admissible localization domain/reference square and prescribed return flow. Choose one nonnegative smooth cosine time coefficient supported near the end of the first replayed pause.

Recorded check: Lemma 4.2, p. 23, assumes \(g,h\in L^2((0,1);H^{m-1})\) but asserts convergence in \(H^m\), uniformly over bounded sets of those forces.

nu=m=1, w0=0 in H2, zero prescribed mean path apart from the actual return drift y(t); g,h in L2_t H0 with zero spatial means. Set a(t)=integral y, a(1) in (2pi Z)^2.

Recorded check: Theorem 5.1, pp. 27–28, asserts that one collection \((\zeta_l)_{l=1}^N\subset L^2(0,1)\) can be fixed so that \(w_\delta(\delta)\to w_1\) in \(H^k\) as \(\delta\to0\) for…

k=2, w0=0, h=0, nu=1, U=0 and target w1=sum n^-4 sin(nx1), which has zero mean and belongs to H3 but not H4.

Recorded check: The sufficient construction in Remark 2.5, p. 9, allows functions that are zero as \(L^2\) elements.

T=1,n=1 and D={d_j} countable dense without repetitions; phi(t)=sum 2^-j 1_{t=d_j}.

repair.content:
Multiply both correction coefficients by K, or divide both profiles by c=integral chi.

Restrict to a class with uniform C H^{m+1} bounds on the transported solution and uniform integrability of the h-tail energy.

Use tolerance-dependent controls; for a fixed smooth control, the correct limit of the error norm is ||v(1)-w1||H2.

Use psi_j(t)=sum 2^-n 1_{t>d_jn} on pairwise disjoint dense sets.
